texts.pool: aicli guard: refused '{cmd}'. A recursive read over {root} (the Unraid share filesystem) can freeze this server. Run it on the pool path, which holds the same files: {pool}. Reading one named file under {root} is fine.
texts.array: aicli guard: refused '{cmd}'. A recursive read over {root} (the Unraid share filesystem) can freeze this server. This share is also on the array disks, so no single pool path holds all of its files. Search a smaller named folder, use find -maxdepth 1, or ask a person.
texts.network: aicli guard: refused '{cmd}'. {root} is a network mount; a recursive read there is slow and can hang. Name a smaller folder, or ask a person.
texts.ancestor: aicli guard: refused '{cmd}'. A walk from {path} goes into /mnt/user and the network mounts. Add -xdev (find), -x (du) or --one-file-system (rg, fd) to stay on one file system, or name the folder you need.
